name: The dead torch-bulb circuit
subject: practical_science
brief: In the physics practical every group wired the same torch-bulb circuit and yours is the only one that stays dark. The lab technician hands out one spare bulb, cell or lead at a time and writes each one down, so every swap costs you a visit to the store cupboard. You are the experimenter: choose which tests to run, and run only as many as the period allows.

causes.name: A crocodile clip is not gripping

tests.name: Fit a bulb from a working circuit
Fit a cell from a working circuit
Read the meter for continuity across the switch and the leads
Bridge the switch with a spare wire
Re-seat and tighten every clip, then close the switch

note: A Class XI physics practical (INDIA_WORLD_BIBLE.md, school bible). Parts are the scarce resource, so every swap costs a unit more. The experimenter's discount applies to the meter, so the cheap way to the clip is a reading and a bridge. Continuity narrows the fault to two causes and a bridged switch settles which.
